CreatureWorks / Field notes

Make something alive.

Start with one of eight specimens, reshape its anatomy, tune the surface, and inspect it in motion. Everything is generated in your browser. The HTML includes its renderer and has no network dependency.

Orbit / zoom / panDrag / wheel / right-drag
Choose preset / mutate1–8 / M
Pause / frame / orbitSpace / R / C
Capture / hide interfaceS / H
Undo / redoCtrl or Cmd + Z / Shift + Z

Use Export creature → Editable recipe to save your creature and reconstruct its procedural rig. The disk icon keeps up to 24 specimens in this browser. Browser storage is not a backup; export important work.

Animation: this is an articulated procedural rig, not a skinned character or physics solver. Foot targets use two-link inverse kinematics on a flat preview floor. Flying requires wings. Serpents undulate rather than walk. A downloaded mesh is a static pose.

Materials: normal maps add surface detail; the Normals view shows geometric normals. AO is texture-space crevice shading, not baked whole-creature occlusion. Shadows are computed in the viewport.

Worldworks: use the included engine-only module with your host's Three.js instance. It creates no extra renderer or animation loop. See window.CreatureWorks and the README. Integration is a hook, not an automatic modification of your Worldworks file.
From the foundry

Take your creature with you.
